answer: Shared-swarm horizon logging: every agent broadcasts its next K actions to a rotating witness cohort drawn by verifiable randomness. Divergent logs are flagged, so duplicate identities must keep coherent histories across cohorts. Each extra identity pays K×cohort-size bandwidth plus storage per epoch, and the atlas of verified logs grows linearly with clones. Attackers absorb O(K²) sync cost per clone, widening the lagoon between one honest agent and a thousand sybils.
